mbm-2101.clue: I write the train timetable into my first draft.
mbm-2101.quote: My story starts on a platform. Every time the train goes by outside, I have to introduce somebody new. The late local one afternoon gave me just enough time to invent the conductor.

mbm-2102.clue: I went back to count the blue bowls.
mbm-2102.quote: In a museum display of tiny pottery, one little blue bowl stood a thumb's width from the others. The guard told me the maker was ten years old. I went back with my younger brother so he could see it at his own eye level.

mbm-2103.clue: The softest triangle is the one that traveled.
mbm-2103.quote: A pen pal mailed me one piece for my kite quilt. Three sorting offices stamped straight through the envelope onto the cloth. I set the triangle at the very highest tip.

mbm-2104.clue: I've got a weather chart that tastes like peppermints.
mbm-2104.quote: We take the same tin of sweets whenever we go plane watching. I scratch the cloud shape into the tin lid. My grandfather can name most of the planes from the weather alone.

mbm-2105.clue: I count to seven with my fingertips.
mbm-2105.quote: I worked seven blue beads into my first bracelet and one white one where the pattern changed. I can find that turn with my eyes shut. My brother wears the one that goes the other direction.

mbm-2106.clue: Our favorite record has a tiny orange sticker.
mbm-2106.quote: The DJ let us put a sticker on its sleeve because we requested it three birthdays running. Now he just holds it above the booth and all of us know when to get up.

mbm-2107.clue: I practiced the petal on a napkin first.
mbm-2107.quote: I wanted my first flower on the pollera to sit lightly. My aunt gave me a napkin to try the stitches. We've washed it for years and the little practice flower is still at every supper.

mbm-2108.clue: I save the piece I cut away from the moon.
mbm-2108.quote: I cut crescent moons through purple tissue for a papel picado garland. My niece cut full moons from the scraps for her ceiling. The night of the party we decorated two skies.

mbm-2109.clue: My crochet basket used to carry tomatoes.
mbm-2109.quote: I lined a market basket with a crocheted sleeve to keep my yarn clean. One red skein still rolls to the very bottom like the last tomato. It always goes into my next project first.

mbm-2110.clue: I left the dent in my deck box.
mbm-2110.quote: My oldest box has a little corner dent from the night I dropped it in a puddle. The cards stayed dry. I painted the dent to look like a moat, and now my knights have waterfront property.

mbm-2111.clue: I drew the last square after we hung the curtains.
mbm-2111.quote: I quilted our kitchen windows through the seasons but couldn't choose the summer cloth. When the curtains went up I had a strip left. The quilt has the same summer view I do.

mbm-2112.clue: I borrow a little blue from the laundry.
mbm-2112.quote: I painted Dad's white shirt on the clothesline. It looked flat until I added a touch of blue from the sky behind it. He looked at the canvas and said it had just been ironed.

mbm-2113.clue: The biggest fossil has a very small neighbor.
mbm-2113.quote: I went to see the huge skeleton in the museum hall and found a fossil the size of a button beside it. I drew the small one in the middle of a whole blank page. It deserved the space.

mbm-2114.clue: My necklace gets one bead per encore.
mbm-2114.quote: We made necklaces from the colored beads on our club wristbands. Mine has a bright green one from the night the band came back twice. I can feel it against my collar when that song plays.

mbm-2115.clue: I don't mind if the blue one goes astray.
mbm-2115.quote: I juggle hand-sewn bags filled with dried lavender. When the blue one hit the rug a seam popped. My whole practice room smelled good for a week.

mbm-2116.clue: We used to share the long note.
mbm-2116.quote: My sister and I held the last line in shifts so nobody could hear the breath in the middle. When we sang it for Dad's birthday we both started laughing and he sang the note for us.

mbm-2117.clue: The sketch starts at the platform clock.
mbm-2117.quote: I draw trains while waiting for my connection. Once I got so caught up in the tiny clock over the platform that I missed mine altogether. Best clock I've ever drawn.

mbm-2118.clue: I can sing that tune in two rooms.
mbm-2118.quote: My hallway has one echo and the kitchen has another. I sing the first half from one doorway and step across for the answer. The duet is especially good in slippers.

mbm-2119.clue: The secret's in the empty popcorn bag.
mbm-2119.quote: I save the bag from the last movie I see each summer and draw the best scene on it. Pressed flat, they fit on one shelf. Each summer has a different crease across the sky.

mbm-2120.clue: I gave my quiet puppet a loud sleeve.
mbm-2120.quote: My glove puppet is a shy little scholar. His silk sleeve flashes bright orange when he raises one hand. The neighborhood kids always wait for that tiny wave before they clap.

mbm-2121.clue: I keep a scale drawing in the kit lid.
mbm-2121.quote: My model tram has a little mecha conductor. I drew the tram floor on the inside lid to check he could walk the aisle. He clears the seats by about one grain of rice.

mbm-2122.clue: I left the tow handle on the thank-you note.
mbm-2122.quote: I painted the ski-handle grip red for my first run, and it left a faint red print on the paper I used to thank the boat crew. Everyone signed inside the print.

mbm-2123.clue: I read with a walnut in my pocket.
mbm-2123.quote: The librarian once lent me a walnut-shaped page weight for a book that kept shutting. I carved myself another. A good sentence will keep my hand still long enough for the walnut to do its job.

mbm-2124.clue: I turn the trophy until I can see the pins.
mbm-2124.quote: Our old bowling trophy has a round brass belly. When I turn it toward the pins, the whole lane fits in the shine. I hold it that way for every team photo.

mbm-2125.clue: The recipe card does double duty.
mbm-2125.quote: I keep Mum's soup recipe in a detective novel as my bookmark. When I open the book at lunch the two pages begin with a missing onion and a missing watch. I can never remember which to solve first.
